openQuestions: Existing test updated (assertion timing only): apps/desktop/test/application-work.test.ts 'keeps document work independent when the person types in another app' now advances 1101 ms instead of 101 ms before expecting applicationFrameHide, because the hide is debounced by 1000 ms. The whole apps/desktop/test directory passed inside check:quick (499 files); the single-directory criterion command was run before the last lint-only edit to the new test file and failed only on that 101 ms assertion, which is now fixed.

Previous finding 1 (native 150 ms poll orders the frame out): Frame.swift restarts its hide timer on every applicationFrame request, so track() now re-sends applicationFrame on every 100 ms poll while the frame is held visible. The native timer therefore does not get to fire and the 1000 ms debounce in TypeScript is what decides the hide. This rests on one poll cycle (100 ms plus three host round trips) staying under 150 ms; a host stalled for more than about 50 ms can still let the native poll hide the frame during a foreground loss until the next poll re-shows it. Removing that fully needs a Swift change, which is out of scope. Not verified on a real Mac: only with a fake host that records request times (max gap under 150 ms).

The keep-alive means applicationFrame (setFrame + orderFrontRegardless on the border panel) goes out about every 100 ms. The native timer already did exactly that every 150 ms, so the ordering rate is about the same as before, but it is not zero. If the reviewer wants no repeated orderFrontRegardless at all, that also needs Swift.

Previous finding 2: show() no longer sends applicationFrame when the frame is already up for the same window in the foreground; it sends only when entering a window, when the frame was hidden, or during a held foreground loss.
A minimized window gets no keep-alive (the native call could fail on it), so the native poll hides its border within 150 ms while applicationFrameHide and the overlay status follow after 1000 ms.

Web preview cards now use a per-lane key so a navigation does not remount the card; with no DOM test environment this is asserted through the key function previewSlot, not a mounted tree. PreviewCard.tsx is unchanged.
Windows: the per-action reveal used to re-assert the topmost level; now only the existing 5 s reassert timer does.
